summary: New Jersey delegate to the Continental Congress and Ohio pioneer, father-in-law of President William Henry Harrison; linked to John by marriage through his wife Anna Tuthill.
bio: John Cleves Symmes was born on Long Island on 21 July 1742. He represented New Jersey in the Continental Congress, served as a judge, and became a pioneer of the Northwest Territory through the land grant known as the Symmes Purchase. He died at North Bend, Ohio, on 26 February 1814. He was the father-in-law of President William Henry Harrison and the great-grandfather of President Benjamin Harrison. He is connected to John by marriage rather than by blood: the family's line runs through his wife, Anna Tuthill.

media.note: John Cleves Symmes (July 21, 1742 – February 26, 1814) was a delegate to the Continental Congress from New Jersey, and later a pioneer in the Northwest Territory.  He was also the father-in-law of President William Henry Harrison and, thereby, the great-grandfather of President Benjamin Harrison.
